en.html:
The iron giant had gone silent.
A deep horizontal crack lay open across it. Under the moon it glittered: a mountain of scrap, all its greatness finished.

My legs were not obeying. I made them climb anyway, dragged myself up that heap and hauled out the Rokuhara-standard dragoon slumped in the crack as though he had spilled from it. The man who had piloted the giant was unconscious.

Him I dumped on the ground. I looked inside. Beyond layer upon layer of crossing girders, shut in a cage, they were huddled together.

Nobody moved.
Pressed against one another. Still.

A block of ice slid down inside my chest, along the breastbone.
Call their names. Find out whether they are alive. Such a simple thing to do. Fear was not letting even the voice come.

山となり果てている。

こぼれたような格好で項垂れる六波羅制式の竜騎兵を
引き摺り出す。

いう単純な作業が、恐怖によって阻止されている。

Tall, with so much muscle that the uniform appeared to be resisting him from outside. The face, however, was pale and handsome, almost delicate: quite a different proposal from the body. en.html:
Understood.
Very thoroughly understood.

This was the man.
This was his justice.

The Anglo-Saxon peoples had, one might almost say, conquered the world. For him this was not merely strategy and technology doing their work. It was Manifest Destiny: God had selected one special people, and conquest was their appointed fate. Such believers were not rare. Nor was the belief difficult to grasp.

Bhagwan ne chun liya. God has chosen them. After that, whatever their hands are doing becomes God's intention also. A very accommodating heaven. The army advances, and the Almighty is found marching immediately behind, carrying the explanation.

Only, to bring his values anywhere near a Yamato man's, each would have to walk some five hundred light-years toward the other.
For this much mutual understanding, time was unfortunately not available.

There was a mission we had to carry through.
We—Muramasa.

Dying here was not allowed. Getting drunk on the prospect of a beautiful tragic end was also a use of time we could not afford. Some ugly way of staying alive: that was what I had to find.

I examined the encirclement.
Excellent work. Water would not leak out of it. An ant would have to surrender.

By air, especially, there was no hope. They already held the sky. However I considered it, I could see no prospect of taking off without being shot down at once.

Ground was the only way. Tanks and infantry would hold me in place; the Grapplers, made for low-altitude combat, would strike from above while I was occupied. Naturally that would be their method. Could I spoil it?

Fight while moving. Choose the moment, break away, come back here. Secure the Haya boy and his family, rejoin our companions, get out.
That was the required sequence. Very easy to arrange as sentences.

Possibly a little harder than climbing Fuji naked in midwinter.

The blond giant must have noticed my movement and what it meant. He moved.

His two-handed greatsword swept a cross through the air.
He roared.

戻り芳養少年一家の身柄を確保、そして仲間と合流し、
脱出を果たす。
　こちらが踏むべき手順はそのようになる。

ようにも思えた。

...Was he actually proposing single combat?

He could hardly have heard the question inside my head. But his next words came in that same level voice.
